sections.what_happened: Israel escalated attacks on south Lebanon on Saturday: NNA reported a strike on a home in Ansar killed 7 and wounded 3 — worst toll since the June lull — plus strikes on the Ali al-Taher ridge (Nabatieh) and a valley strike between Ansar and Zarariyeh, 'the first at this geographical depth since the ceasefire two months ago'. Saturday's escalation followed IDF evacuation warnings for 20 locations including Nabatieh, urging residents north of the Zahrani river. L'Orient reported artillery shelling and demolitions continuing overnight Saturday into Sunday morning (Wadi Zibqine, Mansouri, Wadi Slouqi, Mayfadoun, Qantara, Beit Yahoun, Zawtar Sharqieh) and olive farmers expelled from Kfar Shuba after refusing Israeli harvest conditions. Al Jazeera cites Lebanon's Health Ministry: at least 10 killed Saturday; death toll since March 2 at 2,659 with 8,183 injured.
sections.what_verified: NNA reporting carried by citizen.digital and Al Jazeera; Naharnet on the 20-town evacuation warnings; L'Orient overnight shelling details consistent with the Saturday wave. Israel's stated justification (targeting Hezbollah) per its military; casualty figures Lebanese-official, unverified independently.
sections.what_disputed: Israeli military has said strikes target Hezbollah infrastructure (Ali al-Taher ridge described as 'underground terror infrastructure'); no independent confirmation of casualty split civilian/combatant. Hezbollah said Friday its fighters confronted Israeli forces near Majdal Zoun — the fighting is mutual, not one-sided.
sections.why_matters: Rolling-update feedstock for the next Lebanon Short: Saturday's 7-killed Ansar strike is the worst single toll since the June lull — IDF issued 20-town evacuation warnings before hitting. Side-of-truth framing: report the Lebanese-official toll with source tags, carry Israel's stated rationale, note the Tampa/Oct 20 talks backdrop. No fresh 'breaking' hook on its own.
